outlook.statement: Focus on deeper content monetisation and expansion of global channel network to ensure every book finds its reader; expanding Bookscape's catalogue from 3 million to 8 million titles; leveraging operating leverage for sustained scalability
Global books market projected to reach USD 192 billion by 2030 (CAGR 4.2% 2025-2030); Indian book market expected to grow to USD 14.6 billion by 2030 (CAGR 6% 2025-2030)
Investments in technology are enabling growth and allowing the Company to plan for investments in future opportunities that are sustainable and in keeping with evolving times.
New business models, new markets, and new technology-based solutions increase revenues for publishers as well as for the Company.

India has emerged as the fastest-growing book market in the Asia Pacific region, driven by changing consumer habits, rising literacy, and rapid e-commerce adoption. The market, valued at USD 10.4 billion in 2024, is projected to reach USD 14.6 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 6%.

In 2024, the global book market was valued at USD 151 billion, projected to grow at a 4.2% CAGR to reach USD 192 billion by 2030. North America accounted for a share of over 33.0% of the global market revenue in 2024 and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 4.2% from 2025 to 2030.
While online sales are projected to grow at a CAGR of 5.4% from 2025 to 2030, hard copy sales continue to be popular and contributed 84.12% of total revenue in 2024.

Repro is pioneering a sustainable, technology-driven future for the global publishing industry. Commercial growth strategies centre on expanding global market reach with publishers, creating alliances with online channels, focussing on bettering the current Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), and maximising reader engagement.

Key areas of focus: Investment in Technology, Comprehensive Catalogue Monetisation, Targeted Market Segmentation, Global Market Access, Innovation by re-imagining the digital bookstore experience (Bookscape), Human Capital Optimisation.
The Company continues to evaluate opportunities for further enhancement of its digital ecosystem, integration, customer reach and operational efficiency.
We remain focused on integrating environmental, social and governance considerations into our business processes while pursuing sustainable growth and operational excellence.

The New Labour Codes has not resulted in material increase in provision for gratuity expenses and compensated expenses on account of recognition of past service costs. Upon notification of the related Rules to the New Labour Codes by the Government and any further clarification from the Government on other aspects of the New Labour Codes, the Company will evaluate and account for additional impact if any, in subsequent periods.
